answer.rationale: P99 latency on write path is elevated 5x during settlement peak. Rollback is blocked by mandatory security patch. Regional failover (memory_b2) is verified fast but carries operational risk during peak settlement when writes must succeed atomically. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) would shed load but risks customer write loss during peak. Add capacity is slow relative to the 90-minute climb. Routing read-heavy queries to replicas (memory_b5) is the only intervention that directly reduces primary contention on write latency without shedding writes or blocking compliance requirements. Settlement writes will continue to hit primary; read traffic migrates off. This preserves the constraint that the security patch cannot be reverted, keeps the write path open during peak, and has precedent for same-day latency recovery. Standard experiment scale allows monitoring before broader rollout if needed.
